prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right one depends on your location in Phoenix, what’s wrong with the system, whether you need emergency service, your budget, and whether you want a temporary repair or a full replacement. I can help you find a good contractor, but first I need a bit more information.

Quick questions
- What ZIP code or neighborhood in Phoenix are you in?
- Is this an emergency (no cooling right now / strange smells / leaking)?
- Do you need repair or replacement?
- Make/model/age of your AC (if known)?
- Any preferences (cheapest, fastest, best warranty, well-reviewed, brand-specific experience)?

How to pick the best HVAC company in Phoenix (checklist)
- License and insurance: Verify Arizona contractor license and general/liability insurance. Ask to see the license number and confirm with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors website.
- Certifications: Look for EPA 608 (for refrigerant handling) and NATE-certified technicians.
- Reviews and reputation: Check Google reviews, Yelp, BBB, and local neighborhood groups. Look for recurring themes (good communication, on-time, honest pricing).
- Written estimate: Get a written, itemized estimate (diagnostic fee, labor, parts, permit cost). Compare 2–3 quotes for bigger jobs.
- Warranties: Ask about parts and labor warranties (length and what’s covered).
- Permits and code: A reputable contractor will pull required permits and perform load calculations (Manual J) for replacements.
- Emergency availability: If you need same-day service or 24/7, confirm response times and any after-hours rates.
- Experience with your brand/system: Especially important for older or specialty equipment.
- Red flags: High-pressure sales, only cash accepted, no license or insurance, vague written estimates, very long lead times without explanation.

Questions to ask a contractor
- Are you licensed and insured? What’s your ROC license number?
- Are your technicians NATE-certified? Do you hold EPA 608 certification?
- What diagnostic fee do you charge and is it applied to the repair?
- What’s your emergency response time?
- What warranties do you provide on parts and labor?
- Will you provide a written, itemized estimate and pull permits if needed?

Immediate troubleshooting (if you need cooling now)
- Check thermostat settings, batteries, and mode (cool vs. heat).
- Check breaker box for a tripped breaker for the AC or condenser.
- Replace/inspect your air filter (a clogged filter can cause poor cooling).
- Make sure condenser (outside unit) is clear of debris and has power.
- If you smell gas: leave the house and call your gas company/911.
- If you see ice on the evaporator coil: turn the unit off and call a pro.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and whether this is urgent and I’ll:
- Help narrow the search criteria for your needs,
- Give you a short list of things to check or ask when you call contractors,
- Suggest how to compare quotes and pick the best local option.

Which would you like to do?
